how-often-to-post-on-each-platform.html.text:
Interview Content Studio · guide

How often to post on each platform, and how to fill the calendar from one interview

"Post every day everywhere" is advice almost nobody can follow for long. A better question is how much you can keep up, on which platforms, with the hours you really have, and where the ideas come from. This page sets out the starting rhythms the studio uses, how it fits them to your time, and how one interview supplies a month of material.

Starting rhythms and limits, per format

Each format has a floor (the least that keeps it alive) and an ideal, both counted over four weeks, and a rough number of minutes per piece when you edit a draft from the studio rather than start from a blank page (filming included for video). These are the studio's starting assumptions, not measured benchmarks. Try them for a month and move them to what you can sustain and what gets replies.

Platform-set limits: X posts 280 characters (each link counts as 23), Threads 500, Bluesky 300, LinkedIn posts 3,000, Instagram captions 2,200 with at most 30 hashtags, Facebook posts 63,206, YouTube titles 100 and descriptions 5,000, Reddit titles 300 and text posts 40,000, Pinterest titles 100 and descriptions 500. A "~" marks a guideline rather than a hard limit (search titles, meta descriptions, email subjects), where the studio warns instead of cutting. Everything else (hook length, slide and beat counts, a 2,200-character TikTok caption) is the studio's own conservative choice. Platforms change their limits, so check before relying on one.

Fitting the plan to your hours

The studio turns your hours a week into a minutes budget for four weeks and spends it in three passes: first one piece of each platform's main format (cheapest platforms first, so more of them get covered), then every format up to its floor, then up towards its ideal, one piece at a time, cheapest first in each round. Whatever the budget cannot reach is listed as "not this month", not silently dropped, so you can choose between adding time and dropping a platform.

Worked example, from the studio itself: LinkedIn, Instagram and a newsletter at 3 hours a week.

FormatPieces in 4 weeksPer week
LinkedIn post61.5
Instagram feed post61.5
Instagram reel51.3
Instagram carousel30.8
Newsletter issue20.5

That uses about 176 minutes of the 180 a week. Every format is at or above its floor and below its ideal, so extra time would go to the cheapest formats first: LinkedIn posts, then Instagram feed posts.

Where a month of ideas comes from: one interview

The interview asks for raw material, not posts: who you serve and their problem in their words, three to five real stories with what you learned, opinions people would argue with, advice you give again and again, results you can show, and the one thing you want people to do next. Each answer becomes an angle. The calendar gives every day one theme, so the same story appears as a hook on X, a short post with its lesson on LinkedIn, a 30 to 60 second script for Reels and TikTok, and a fuller version in the newsletter, each in the shape that platform expects. Roughly one piece in five carries your offer; the rest give value with no ask. Reddit drafts never carry one.

Because the drafts are assembled only from your answers, they cannot contain a result you did not give. If you add AI on your own key, the model is held to the same rule: a rewrite that adds a number not in your interview is thrown away.

Questions

How many times a week should a small business post?

As many times as it can keep up for months, on the platforms where its customers are. A rhythm you can hold beats a burst you abandon. The studio starts each format at a floor and an ideal rhythm, then fits them to your hours and tells you which platforms your time cannot cover.

How do I repurpose one piece of content across platforms?

Start from one idea, such as a story, an opinion or a tip, and reshape it rather than copy it: a one-line hook for X, Threads and Bluesky, a short story with a lesson for LinkedIn, a 30 to 60 second script for Reels, TikTok and Shorts, slides for a carousel, and a fuller version for a newsletter or article. The studio gives each day one theme and drafts it for every platform posting that day.

Start the interview

Interview Content Studio · free · runs in your browser

Turn one interview into a month of content for every platform

Answer a guided interview about your brand, business or topic: who you serve, the problem you solve, your real stories, opinions, advice and results. The studio sizes a posting plan to the hours you actually have, lays out a 4-week calendar, and drafts every piece in the shape each platform wants: posts for X, Threads, Bluesky, LinkedIn and Facebook, Instagram captions and carousels, scripts for Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts, YouTube outlines, newsletter issues, blog articles, Reddit and Pinterest posts, and podcast clips.

Drafts are built only from your own answers, so nothing is made up. Your answers stay in this browser and nothing is uploaded. AI rewriting is optional and runs on your own key or a model on your own computer. The studio never posts anything for you.

1. Interview2. Plan and calendar3. Drafts4. Export

1. The interview

Run as many interviews as you like: one per brand, product, client or topic. Each is saved separately in this browser.

Save, move or share your interviews

Answers are kept in this browser's local storage. Download a copy to keep them safe, move them to another device, or run the command-line version.

2. How much to post, and when

Answer the interview (or as much as you can), then build your plan.

PlatformFormatPer weekMinutes eachWhy this rhythm

    These rhythms are this tool's starting points, not measured benchmarks: a floor and an ideal per format, fitted to your hours with the cheapest formats first. Try them for a month and adjust to what you can keep up and what gets replies.

    Your 4-week calendar

    3. Drafts for every slot

    Each draft is assembled from your answers and fitted to the platform's limits. Edit any draft in place; your edits are what gets copied and exported.

    Optional: rewrite drafts in your voice with your own AI key

    AI is off unless you set it up here. It sends your interview answers and the drafts straight from this browser to the provider you pick; your key stays in this browser and is never sent to us. The model is told to use only facts from your interview, and any AI draft that adds a number not in your interview is thrown away. If a call fails, the built-in draft stays. A model on your own computer (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) needs no key and nothing leaves your machine: start Ollama with OLLAMA_ORIGINS=https://duncan-haywood.github.io, or turn on CORS in LM Studio's server settings.

    Build your plan to see drafts here.

    4. Export

    This tool does not post anywhere. Review every draft, follow each platform's rules, label AI-generated content where a platform requires it (TikTok, YouTube and Meta ask creators to disclose realistic AI-generated or altered media), and do not use it for spam, fake accounts or fake reviews.

    The CSV has one row per draft with the columns date, platform, format, title and text, which most schedulers and spreadsheets can import (map the columns on import).

    Run it from the command line

    Zero dependencies, Node 18+. Feed it the file from "Download all interviews".

    node cli.mjs studio.json --format plan
node cli.mjs studio.json --start 2026-11-02 --format csv > calendar.csv
node cli.mjs studio.json --interview "Bakery launch" --format md

    Questions people ask

    How do I turn one interview into content for every platform?

    Answer the guided interview: who you are, who you serve, their problem, three to five real stories, your opinions, your advice, results you can show, and your offer. The studio turns each answer into a different angle and reshapes it for each platform: a short post for X, Threads and Bluesky, a longer post for LinkedIn, a script for Reels, TikTok and Shorts, slides for a carousel, a newsletter issue and a blog article.

    How often should I post on each platform?

    There is no single right number. The studio starts from a floor and an ideal rhythm for each format, then fits them to the hours a week you say you have, cheapest formats first, and tells you which platforms your time cannot cover. Treat the numbers as a starting point for a month, then adjust to what you can keep up and what gets replies.

    Does it make up facts or results?

    No. The built-in drafts are assembled only from your own answers, with short connecting phrases. If you turn on AI, it is told to use only facts from your interview, and any AI draft containing a number that is not in your interview is thrown away and the original draft kept.

    Do I need an AI key?

    No. Every draft works without one. Optionally, add your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or OpenAI-compatible key, or point it at a model on your own computer (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp), to rewrite drafts in your voice. The key stays in your browser and goes only to the provider you pick.

    Does it post for me?

    No. It never posts anywhere. Copy drafts one by one, or export a CSV with date, platform, format, title and text to import into the scheduler you already use, then review and post yourself.
